featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Response to the Allegation:

We would like to clarify the situation regarding the unfortunate demise of the complainant's mother, who was admitted to our care facility in a comatose state. At the time of admission, her brother was present and fully informed by our team about her critical condition, including the possibility of her passing at any time, as had already been communicated by their treating doctor.

Due to their inability to manage her care at home, the family opted for admission into our center, acknowledging that all medical expenses arising during her stay would be borne by them. This was clearly explained and agreed upon at the time of admission.

Regarding the unfortunate event of her passing, we must clarify that it is standard and respectful practice to request the family to make timely arrangements for the body. We are a care facility, not a mortuary, and it is neither practical nor appropriate for us to retain the deceased beyond a reasonable time. Suggesting that we should not have asked for the body to be taken reflects a misunderstanding of protocol and responsibilities.

The billing shared with the family post-demise was for the medical services rendered during the patient's stay, which is routine and transparent. Expecting the facility to delay or waive the bill is unreasonable. Immediate communication was necessary, as deferring the matter would only have created confusion and logistical difficulties later.

It is also important to note that his  brother visited regularly, was in consistent communication with our staff, and expressed gratitude for the care provided after the patient’s demise. In contrast, the complainant was rarely present, did not make regular inquiries about her condition, and is now raising concerns nearly six months later.

We understand that grief can manifest in various ways, and we extend our sincere sympathies once again. However, public accusations that ignore facts and misrepresent the situation are unfair and disheartening to the caregivers who strive to support families during such sensitive times.

We remain committed to transparency, compassion, and continual improvement in the services we provide.

My mother had developed a paralytic stroke and hence is immobile since the past few months. The caretaker at Divine Elder Care said she started developing Bedsores before she was discharged (which was not the case). The bedsores started in her lower back area after she was admitted to Divine Elder Care. They assured me they would be dressing daily on the bedsore which again was not happening that turned the grade 1 bedsore into a grade 4 bedsore. A paralytic stroke patient usually requires physiotherapy immediately to be back on their feet, I was assured the physiotherapist would start physiotherapy ASAP but later found out they're out of physiotherapist. Lastly, regarding financial transactions PLS BE VERY VERY CAREFUL AND READ ALL THE FINEPRINTS CAREFULLY. My mother was admitted with the following charges -
Rs 25000 - Monthly charges
RS 15000 - onetime admission charges for all patients
Rs 5000 - Deposit charges
Rs 3000 - Air Bed charges
We discharged her within 22 days of admission as I was worried of her health getting deteriorated more if we keep her at this facility.
They charged us additional Rs 25000 for another month as their admission paper fine print reads "Divine Elder Care should be notified 30 days in advance of Discharge " . We found this condition super weird, like why on earth would any facility require so much discharge notice.(This condition only exists to mint money out of customers)
Apart from this additional Rs 25000 charges they also charged Rs 14000 as bedsore dressing and doctor fees. I understand the Dr Fees, but I do not find any evidence of dressing been done on a daily basis.
So guys be super cautious before admitting your dear ones to this facility, I do not think this is a charitable trust at all (I wish I could post the bedside images that my mom sustained, it was really in a  deplorable state)

featured_reviews.name: aadvanis
featured_reviews.review_text:
I was born in Mumbai and now live in the U.K. and my father has lived here his whole life… in May he was diagnosed with a rare and aggressive cancer and we jointly decided he needed to shift to a elder care home… I came in May and visited many places…. None of them hit the mark…. Some were too clinical and hospital like, some were understaffed and looked really depressing, some were too far out of Mumbai to be practical and then finally I visited Olive in Vashi.
Immediately upon meeting the centre manager Mr Ashher and the psychologist Subhashree, I knew I’d found the right place… their warmth and enthusiasm was evident within minutes of my arrival… i had a look around and very quickly i realised my prayers had been answered…. We were racing against the clock… my father was given 2 months prognosis and he was unable to move around so I had to visit the homes by myself…. We agreed when I found the right place he would come and take the final call…. I went home and told him about the home, and we should take a look…. He said no need, I can make out by the way you speak about the place that it will be suitable…. And from there he instructed me to pack his bag…
I stayed for about 10’days while he settled in and I was dreading my pending return to the U.K. as I have a family and a business to run.
Upon returning I was in touch daily, the home sent me pictures daily, as my father weakened and was unable to use his phone, they facilitated all the calls from their personal phone…. The two personal caretakers, Raj and Tushar were pivotal in all this happening… anytime I needed something, any special request to ensure his comfort, a quick WhatsApp and it was as good as done… the doctors were also fantastic…. Extremely thorough, with daily reports…. Every decision they made would be authorised by me first…. And no stones were left unturned…. In the final days his level of treatment and care was increased and they managed the situation also…. No need to go to a hospital and disrupt my father as by now shifting him would be very stressful…. Finally my father found his peace and this is when the Olive family rose up and supported me in my darkest hour…. Being from abroad I had no idea what to do…. And on top of processing the emotions of huge loss, at this point even remembering my name and date of birth would have been tricky…. They organised everything from tedious paperwork right down to the crematorium…. Even now I’m no longer a client I just know if I need any help, a quick WhatsApp and it will be done….
Thank you team Olive… you looked after my father like he was part of the family…. You have helped me through what I can only describe as one of the toughest moments in my life…. You’re a credit to your industry and each and every one of you have shown nothing but empathy and pure class.
May you always be blessed and may you always continue to bless other families in their moment of need.
Om Shanti

Choosing a place for my parent was one of the hardest decisions I've had to make, but The Wisdom Club has been a total blessing.

The central location is also a huge plus, making it so easy for me to drop by and visit regularly.

The first thing you notice is how clean and peaceful it feels and it’s got a genuine warmth.

What first gave us peace of mind were the pre-joining meetings with Dr. Prem n Dr Manasa who were so sincere and they wanted to learn about my parent’s personal life story and our specific situation, not just the medical numbers. That level of care is rare.

The daily curated activities keep the atmosphere lively, and the food is a real standout with the Maharaj who prepares simple, tasty, home-cooked meals making it feel so much more personal.

The staff are also incredible, so patient and always smiling even at busy times but a special shout-out to Seema! Her bubbly nature adds so much life and joy to the place.

It is such a relief to see my parent treated with this much love and dignity & just so grateful to have found this place and highly recommend  The Wisdom club to anyone looking for elder care in Mumbai.

My father stayed at The Wisdom Club for a month after his hip surgery. He had suffered a fall and needed to be admitted to the hospital immediately. One of the best decisions we made was bringing him to The Wisdom Club post his surgery.

The atmosphere there truly sped up his recovery. It was calm, positive and reassuring in every way. A big thank you to Dr. Prem and Dr. Manasa, along with the wonderful caregiving and nursing staff, for their constant care and support. The Wisdom Club truly stands apart and, in my experience, beats any nursing home facility or setup. Deeply grateful for the care my father received here!

featured_reviews.name: PRATIKSHA BANE
featured_reviews.review_text:
I took my mother to The Wisdom Club for physiotherapy sessions, and the experience has been wonderful. The sessions never felt like a “task”. They were engaging and even fun. Dr. Manasa has a rare ability to keep patients motivated while seamlessly ensuring that all the required exercises are covered.

My mother earlier struggled to stay consistent with physiotherapy, but here she continued her sessions regularly and showed rapid improvement in her mobility. She is now able to walk better and feels much more confident in her movement.

Kudos to the entire team at The Wisdom Club for the care, encouragement and for keeping such a positive environment. Highly recommended for physiotherapy and elder care.

featured_reviews.name: Steffi Evelikar
featured_reviews.review_text: I have been regularly visiting The Wisdom Club with my father for his physiotherapy sessions with Dr.Manasa. And I couldn’t be more happier. featured_reviews.name: PinnedCloud
featured_reviews.review_text:
My mother stayed at The Wisdom Club for 21 days while I was travelling and she had a truly positive experience. She often spoke about the warmth of the staff, the comfort of the facility and how well she was cared for throughout her stay.

Though she’s quite independent, the team ensured someone was always present to accompany her from her bed to the bathroom or for her daily walks. She had no complaints about the fresh, home-style meals prepared by their in-house Maharaj (her only complaint was that she ate more than she usually does at home!).

Before her stay, both of us met Dr.Prem and the staff, who took the time to understand her medical history, daily routine and medications, ensuring a seamless transition.

She enjoyed the guided yoga sessions, escorted walks and creative daily activities like diya painting that made each day engaging and joyful.

If there’s one area they could strengthen, it’s setting up smoother communication systems, well-defined processes for different situations in the exploration phase and learning to say “no” when needed. They’re a young, growing organisation and I’m confident they’ll get there.

I had checked several respite and assisted-care centres for seniors in Mumbai before choosing The Wisdom Club. Like many elderly Indians, my mother wasn’t keen on staying in one, but by the end, she told them, “I’ll be back when my daughter travels again.” That says it all.
